revisions.note: v2 and v3 are unchanged. This revision repairs a configuration value that made a subsystem unreachable, before any eval row exists, and records the one eval sample a probe ever queried.
changes: budgets.crgQueryMs 300 -> 993: 300 ms is below the observable floor of `code-review-graph impact` (p99 662 ms over 44 calls on the three pinned sources), so the query timed out on every live row and the tier fell back to the static ladder. The graph has therefore never taken part in a live measurement, including the fit run
the value is derived mechanically: ceil(p99 x 1.5) from the latency table below. No tier was consulted while choosing it, and no tier was computed before it was written
the tier boundaries (tier0.filesMax = 3, tier1.filesMax = 10), the change unit (one file per event), the ruleset, the thresholds and staticTier are untouched
frozen.budgets.crg_query_ms pins the new value; preflight refuses a config whose crgQueryMs differs from it
P1-P4 and every previously frozen value are unchanged

probe_touched: [ts-cwe079-0001] - the tier probes queried this eval sample through real semgrep, crg and ocr, so its detector output has been seen. It is not one of the ten staged positives, and no criterion above was changed after the probes ran

revisions.note: v2-v4 are unchanged. This revision writes down what the staged workspace adds, and corrects the reading of B4g against the code, before the run that will quote both.
changes: every positive is staged with 3 importers written by this project: each staged row carries authored_context: true and authored_importers: 3 in run.json, and the same query on the pinned checkouts is recorded per sample below and joined onto the projection

measured before the run: 0 of the 10 measurable positives would be tier 0 unmodified, 10 are already tier >= 1 (lib/insecurity.ts: 96 importers, tier 2). The tier-1 path is therefore not an artefact of the authored importers, which only reproduce in a twenty-file tree what the repository already says

0 of 9 negatives are tier 0 upstream: the low-risk pool is tier 0 in the staged subset only, so line 4 measures the tier-0 path on a subset that dropped its importers, not the share of low-risk changes a real repository keeps below the boundary

the tier is computed on a ~20-file subtree (index build 1.0 s vs 27.9 s for the full juice-shop checkout); impactedNodes <= 20 is easy at that size, so the conclusion is scoped to 'three sources live on a staged subset'

a positive at tier 0 no longer voids the run on sight: semgrep keeps the row (it ran), AOR drops it (it did not), the row is named in tier0_despite_projection.json and counted on line 1 as aor_excluded; above 2 of 10 the run is void

B4g reading corrected against src/l2/orchestrator.ts:119: with triage.enabled = false, decideTier returns tier 2 with source none and never queries the graph, so B4g runs AOR on all 19 rows while B4 runs it on the 10 positives. The pairing measures what the ladder excludes; the contingency table is B4-only, so P2 and P4 are B4 measurements and B4g contributes line 4 alone

the projection carries baseline per row and assertStrata checks each baseline against what its own config can produce: B4g must be uniform tier 2 by none, so two baselines staged from one config cannot pass
P1-P4 and every previously frozen value are unchanged

observations.warn_rule: zero-parameter structured decision: severity >= warn, threshold_source = severity_policy

frozen.basis: recorded before the run; the run refuses if config, probe or rows disagree with any value here

cost.basis: one file probe x 2 (preview + scan) x 38 staged rows x 1.5 correction headroom; above it the run stops before staging

budgets.derivation: crgQueryMs = ceil(p99(impact latency) x 1.5) = ceil(662 x 1.5) = 993 ms; measured on the three pinned sources, n = 44, before any tier was computed

latency.method: `code-review-graph impact --repo <pinned checkout> --files <one file>` timed through CrgTriage.analyze, files sampled evenly from `git ls-files`; each repository indexed once with `build --skip-flows`
latency.reading: latency is dominated by process start, not by graph size: 674 tracked files and 10 differ by less than 8%

budgets.invariant: semgrepKillMs 5000 + crgQueryMs 993 = 5993 ms <= callMs 8000 ms, asserted at config load by assertBudgetRelations

staged_context.method: `code-review-graph impact` through the same `CrgTriage.analyze` the plugin calls, on the full pinned checkout of each source, with the triage bounds of the config named below and no authored importers. Each file's bytes are hashed as a git blob and compared with the dataset's `origin.blob_sha`, so the answer belongs to the pinned revision rather than to whatever tree was on disk.
staged_context.range_sentence: tier-1 path verified on a workspace where the written file has 3 importers; of the 10 upstream files used, 0 would be tier 0 unmodified, 10 would already be tier >= 1 (1 row creates a path that has no upstream counterpart)
